basic_identification.full_title: Plywood for Concrete Shuttering Works — Specification (Fourth Revision)
basic_identification.sector_category: Civil Engineering / Wood and other Lignocellulosic products (approved by the Civil Engineering Division Council and finalized by the Wood and Other Lignocellulosic Products Sectional Committee of the Bureau of Indian Standards)

sectional_committee.name: Wood and Other Lignocellulosic Products Sectional Committee

scope.summary: This standard specifies the requirements for materials, manufacture, dimensions, tolerances, and testing parameters for plywood used in concrete shuttering, formwork, and scaffolding applications. It ensures that the panels can withstand wet concrete loads, alternate wetting and drying conditions, mechanical pouring forces, and repeated construction cycles without structural failure.

amendment_slips.description: Deletes select paragraphs from the foreword; modifies Clause 6.6 to update glue line protection (GLP) treatment and retention definitions; and completely replaces Clause 10.11 to establish a classified preservative retention and service life table for plain (CS), coated (CSC), and film-faced (CSFF) concrete shuttering plywood.

certification_and_marking.standard_type: Product Specification (Wood Panels & Civil Building Materials)
certification_and_marking.certification_status: Strict Statutory Mandatory Certification. Under the 'Plywood and Wooden Flush Door Shutters (Quality Control) Order' (QCO) issued by the Ministry of Commerce and Industry, Government of India, all Plywood for Concrete Shuttering Works must be certified by the Bureau of Indian Standards and carry the mandatory Standard Mark (ISI Mark). Manufacturing, importing, stocking, or selling non-certified shuttering plywood in India is a statutory offense. MSMEs are granted phased transition timelines, and export-only shipments are exempt. Precious metal hallmarking is completely inapplicable to wood building materials.

requirements.detail: Every panel must carry the BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark) along with the manufacturer's registered licence number (CM/L) and standard designation (IS 4990) marked legibly and indelibly on its face or edge.

The shuttering plywood is classified into three distinct types depending on surface finish: a) Type 1 (CS): Plain shuttering plywood; b) Type 2 (CSC): Plywood with polymer/plastic coating; c) Type 3 (CSFF): Plywood with suitable film-faced overlay.
Adhesives used for bonding the veneers must be unextended Boiling Water Proof (BWP) synthetic phenolic resins conforming strictly to IS 848. The use of MR and BWR grades is completely prohibited.

requirements.requirement_type: Preservative Retention and Service Life (Clause 10.11 - Amended)
requirements.detail:
Under Amendment No. 1, the preservative treatment (GLP and core preservation) must comply with the following boundaries:
a) Type 1 (Plain - CS): 
  - With glue line protection (GLP) treatment: Preservative Retention = 0 kg/m³, Service Life = Single time use. 
  - With preservative treatment: Preservative Retention = 4 kg/m³, Service Life = Upto 1 year. 
  - With preservative treatment: Preservative Retention = 6 kg/m³, Service Life = Upto 2 years. 
b) Type 2 (Coated - CSC): 
  - With preservative treatment: Preservative Retention = 0 (with GLP), Service Life = Single time use with Glue line protection (GLP). 
  - With preservative treatment: Preservative Retention = 4 kg/m³, Service Life = Usage beyond single time. 
c) Type 3 (Film Faced - CSFF): Preservative retention is not applicable (marked as '—' in Table 11).
To prevent warping or splitting, the moisture content of the finished board at testing must be seasoned to remain strictly between 5 and 15 percent when tested per IS 1734 (Part 1).
The internal veneer bond must satisfy high dry shear limits: average failing load of minimum 1350 N, and minimum individual load of 1100 N when tested per IS 1734 (Part 4).

The panel must withstand 72 hours of continuous boiling water immersion with zero separation at edges or delamination of plies, and must maintain a wet glue shear failing load of minimum 1000 N (average) / 800 N (minimum individual).

Along the face grain direction, the panel must develop high load-bearing capacity: a) Modulus of Rupture (MOR): Average minimum 50 N/mm² (MPa), Minimum individual 45 N/mm²; b) Modulus of Elasticity (MOE): Average minimum 7500 N/mm² (MPa), Minimum individual 6700 N/mm².

Across the face grain direction, the panel must satisfy: a) Modulus of Rupture (MOR): Average minimum 30 N/mm² (MPa), Minimum individual 27 N/mm²; b) Modulus of Elasticity (MOE): Average minimum 4000 N/mm² (MPa), Minimum individual 3600 N/mm².
The panel must resist tensile tearing forces: minimum 32.5 N/mm² parallel to the grain, and minimum 22.5 N/mm² across the grain, with a combined sum of at least 60.0 N/mm².
The structural panel must offer exceptional anchorage grip when evaluated in accordance with IS 1734: a) Screw holding strength: minimum 1600 N; b) Nail holding strength: minimum 1300 N.
Finished panel dimensions must satisfy: Length tolerance of ±6 mm, width tolerance of ±5 mm, with edge straightness and squareness deviations limited to a maximum of 2 mm per 1000 mm (0.2 percent).

plain_language_summary.summary: IS 4990 : 2024 is the mandatory national Indian Standard specification regulating high-performance concrete shuttering plywood (formwork sheets) used across civil engineering and infrastructure projects to cast concrete slabs, columns, and bridges. Under India's statutory Plywood Quality Control Order (QCO), all shuttering plywood sold or imported in India must carry the BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark). It restricts construction exclusively to Boiling Water Proof (BWP) grade phenolic resins, banning low-grade MR or BWR options. It classifies sheets into Type 1 (Plain - CS), Type 2 (Coated - CSC), and Type 3 (Film Faced - CSFF). Amendment No. 1 (August 2026) updates the standard by introducing classified preservative retention limits and service life ranges (ranging from single-use GLP sheets to durable, 6 kg/m³ preservative-treated panels rated for up to 2 years of service), ensuring that the formwork safely withstands high pouring forces, extreme outdoor weather, and repeated site usage without buckling or delamination.
